transcript:
This, is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has arrived in China for a rare three-way meeting with Russian President
Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
The trio have already taken a photo together at an economic summit in Shenzhen.
Earlier today, President Trump met the leader of the Philippines at the presidential palace
in Manila and beers deep as shivarum has more.
Trump and the U.S. delegation visited the presidential palace in Manila.
With Secretary of State Marco Rubio seated beside him, Trump reaffirmed the U.S. relationship
with the Philippines.
"With this visit, we're building on these ties to make our partnership even closer."
Trump said the two countries were working to improve energy security and expand defense
cooperation.
The president also briefly talked about U.S. actions abroad, saying the U.S. is "doing
very well" in Iran, despite the conflict going on months longer than Trump said it would.
He also spoke of U.S. intervention in Venezuela, calling it a "acquisition."
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, Shenzhen, China.
Officials in the Philippines have released a statement they say they're looking forward
to strengthening bilateral trade with the U.S.
The computer chip maker, Nvidia, has released its latest quarterly earnings.
They're about $115 billion.
That was mostly settled before Jensen Huang stepped down last week as CEO.
Nvidia board officials say they are not going to bring him back.
And PR's John Ruich says Nvidia still faces questions.
"There will be a lot of investigations.
There's an internal investigation that the board is running.
Huang is also set to appear before several congressional committees.
There are allegations that companies like the one run by the Chinese woman that Jensen
Huang reportedly had an affair with were helping China get a hold of banned chips.
That could potentially point to violations of U.S. export controls.
And then, of course, the board is going to choose a new permanent CEO, the chairman,
Harvey Jones, said on the call it would try to make the pick as quickly as possible without
rushing it."
And PR's John Ruich reporting.
Palestinian officials say an elderly woman has been killed in the latest Israeli attack
in the occupied West Bank.
Israeli and Palestinian officials gave conflicting accounts of what happened in Jericho in the
Jordan Valley.
Israel's Lauren Freer reports.
The Palestinian governor of Jericho says Israeli settlers opened fire on unarmed civilians
and that Israeli soldiers took no action to stop them.
Besides the elderly woman who was shot in the head, health officials say 10 other Palestinians
were wounded.
Israel's military says it began with a traffic incident, with a Palestinian vehicle ramming
an Israeli one, and that passengers got out and started fighting.
It says rocks were hurled at Israelis, and that people from both sides were injured.
Israeli soldiers have sealed off the area and say they're investigating.
Jericho is where Israeli settlers have set up several new outposts, which the international
community considers illegal.
Lauren Freer, NPR News, Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
This is NPR.
California officials have blocked the self-driving Waymo cars from operating on state highways.
Now, Waymo has decided to suspend its operations on all freeways across the country.
There are concerns about safety.
California officials say recently three Waymo vehicles drove into an active construction
zone on part of a closed California freeway.
Last year, North Dakota became one of 29 states that limit how much patients with diabetes
have to pay for insulin.
The cap drew bipartisan support.
Senator Noam Levy, with our partner KFF Health News, has the story.
Diabetes is expensive.
Insulin can cost patients hundreds or thousands of dollars, even if they have insurance.
That's why some risk rationing their insulin.
Red states and blue are landing on a common fix.
Cap how much patients have to pay every month for the drug.
Typically, Republicans are more on the free market side of things, Democrats are more supportive
of intervening.
In this case, I think there's broad agreement that this market just wasn't functioning.
That's Republican Sean Cleary.
He's a North Dakota state senator who co-sponsored a state insulin cap.
Congress is now considering a national cap.
That's Noam Levy, with our partner KFF Health News.
After what feels like forever, at least for fans, the video game Gram Theft Auto 6 launches
tomorrow.
This has been a 13-year wait for the latest installment of one of the most popular video
games ever created.
Players in New Zealand will get the first opportunity at midnight local time.
You're listening to NPR.

topics.text: President Trump arrives in China for three-way meeting with Putin and Xi Jinping
Trump meets Philippine leader in Manila, reaffirming ties and expanding energy and defense cooperation
Nvidia reports quarterly earnings after CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid investigations
Palestinian woman killed in Jericho clash; Israeli and Palestinian accounts conflict
California blocks Waymo self-driving cars from state highways after construction zone incidents
